record.original_question: Let a polygon with at least four sides be circumscribed to a circle, and let D consist of its diagonals together with the lines joining the points of contact of two non-adjacent sides. The paper proves that D contains at least three concurrent lines. Determine conditions under which more than three of these lines are concurrent.

evidence.quote: Let's consider a polygon (which has at least 4 sides) circumscribed to a circle, and D the set of its diagonals and the lines joining the points of contact of two non-adjacent sides. Then D contains at least 3 concurrent lines.
2.1. In what conditions there are more than three concurrent lines?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P = A_1 A_2 \cdots A_n$ be a convex polygon with $n \geq 4$ sides that is circumscribed to a circle $\omega$, meaning every side of $P$ is tangent to $\omega$. For each side $A_i A_{i+1}$ let $T_i \in \omega$ denote its point of tangency with $\omega$ (indices taken mod $n$). Define the family of lines
$$D = \{\, A_i A_j : 1 \le i < j \le n,\ |i-j|\not\equiv 1 \pmod{n}\,\} \;\cup\; \{\, T_i T_j : 1 \le i < j \le n,\ |i-j|\not\equiv 1 \pmod{n}\,\},$$
that is, all diagonals of $P$ together with all lines joining tangency points of two non-adjacent sides. It is known that $D$ always contains at least three concurrent lines. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $P$ (and on $\omega$) under which $D$ contains more than three concurrent lines, i.e. four or more lines of $D$ passing through a common point.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct web search did not surface a published characterization of when more than three of these lines are concurrent for general circumscribed polygons with n ≥ 4. Classical related results (Brianchon's theorem for tangential hexagons, Newton's theorem for tangential quadrilaterals) guarantee concurrency of three specific lines but do not address the more-than-three case. No source explicitly resolving this conditional question was located.

status_evidence.title: Tangential polygon - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses tangential polygons and concurrency results such as Brianchon's theorem for tangential hexagons.
status_evidence.claim: Standard concurrency results are limited to specific configurations (3 lines), and no general criterion for additional concurrency is stated.

status_evidence.title: Properties of a Hexagon Circumscribed to a Circle
status_evidence.snippet: Treats concurrency of diagonals and tangency-chord lines in tangential hexagons via Brianchon-type arguments.
status_evidence.claim: Available references address only the basic three-line concurrency, leaving the higher-order concurrency question without a documented resolution.
